title: ICE Issues New Dress Code Banning Plainclothes Operations After Killings and Botched Las Vegas Arrest
excerpt: ICE's Enforcement and Removal Operations division issued a mandatory field dress code, prohibiting jeans, hoodies, and unbranded clothing after a botched arrest in which plainclothes officers in hoodies were filmed at Harry Reid Airport in Las Vegas, following the two July fatal shootings.
content:
On July 21, 2026, The Intercept published a leaked internal ICE memo, confirmed by multiple ICE officers, mandating a new field dress code for deportation officers. The policy, signed by Acting ICE Director David Venturella, required officers to wear readily identifiable ICE attire during all field operations, including khaki or coyote brown tactical pants paired with an ICE polo, and a ballistic vest during high-visibility operations.

The policy was triggered in part by a botched July 13 arrest at Harry Reid International Airport in Las Vegas, where two ICE officers wearing hooded sweatshirts abandoned an attempted arrest as bystanders recorded video — one officer trying to pull his hood down over his face. One ICE official described the scene as looking like a kidnapping. The memo explicitly bans jeans, sweatshirts, hoodies, non-collared shirts, and graphic-print clothing during field operations, and requires an ICE badge to be visible at the time of arrest.

  • The policy came in the wake of two fatal July shootings — in Houston and Biddeford, Maine — in which agents were not wearing body cameras or easily identifiable uniforms.
  • Critics called the dress code "a long-overdue admission that unidentifiable immigration enforcement is dangerous, instills fear, and erodes public trust."
  • ICE did not respond to The Intercept's request for comment on the memo.
